overview.description: Basra is the most popular card game in Egypt and widely played throughout the Levant. It is a 'Fishing' game related to Italian Casino, where players capture cards from a central pool by matching ranks or summing values. The game is named after the 'Basra' (or 'Basra Bonus'), awarded when a player clears the entire table with a single card. With simple math and high-stakes capturing mechanics (including the powerful Jack and 7 of Diamonds), it is a fast-paced game of calculation and memory.

history.origins: Believed to be a direct descendant of the European game 'Casino' mixed with Ottoman-era card traditions. The word 'Basra' likely refers to the city, but in the context of the game, it implies a 'sweep' or total capture.
timeline: 19th Century: Fishing games spread from Italy (Scopa/Casino) to North Africa.
Early 20th Century: 'Al-Basra' becomes a staple in Cairo coffee houses.
Present: The dominant game in Egyptian cafes, often played for the price of tea or shisha.
history.evolution: While the core rules of matching and summing remain constant, regional variants (like the Lebanese 'Ashush') introduce different point values for specific captures.
history.cultural: In Egypt, Basra is played with a theatrical flair—slamming a Jack on the table to 'clean the floor' is a moment of triumph.

setup.dealing: Dealer deals 4 cards to each player and 4 cards face-up to the 'Floor' (middle). If a Jack or 7 of Diamonds appears on the floor during the initial deal, it is buried in the deck and replaced.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing specific cards (Aces, Jacks, 10♦, 2♣), capturing the most cards overall, and earning 'Basra' bonuses for clearing the table.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing one card from their hand. 1. **Match**: If your card matches the rank of a card on the floor (e.g., play 5, take 5), you capture it. 2. **Sum**: If your card equals the sum of several cards on the floor (e.g., play 9, take 4+5), you capture them. 3. **The Jack**: Playing a Jack captures ALL cards on the floor (unless the floor is empty). 4. **The 7 of Diamonds**: In most Egyptian variants, the 7♦ (The Komi) acts like a Jack and captures everything, but serves as a 'Basra' if it captures only cards totaling 10 or less visually (rules vary). 5. **Basra Bonus**: If you capture the *entire* floor with a non-Jack card (matching the last card or summing to it), you score a 'Basra' (+10 points).
keyRules: Jack takes all (but usually doesn't score a Basra bonus unless strict conditions are met).
7 of Diamonds (Komi) is a 'Super Jack' in Egyptian rules.
Capturing cards goes into a face-down score pile.

strategy.basic: Save your Jacks and 7♦ for when the floor is full of cards to maximize your capture count (Carte).
strategy.intermediate: Basra Hunting: If there is a single card on the table (e.g., a 6) and you hold a matching card (a 6), playing it clears the table and awards the massive 10-point Basra. Prioritize this over big sweeping captures.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: If you have no capture, discard a card that is unlikely to give your opponent a Basra. For example, if you know they hold a Queen, don't discard a Queen.
tips: Memorize the point cards (Aces, J, 10♦, 2♣). These are more valuable than bulk captures.
The 7 of Diamonds is the most powerful card—use it wisely.

difficulty.easy: Captures any match it sees. Plays Jacks randomly if no match.
difficulty.medium: Prioritizes point cards (10♦, 2♣). Saves Jacks for tables with 3+ cards.
difficulty.hard: Calculates the 'Basra Probability' of a discard. Will never discard a card that matches a recently played card by the opponent (if known). Counts the 7♦ and Jacks.

considerations: Combinatorial Summation: AI must check subsets of floor cards to find sums equal to hand cards.
End-game handling: Last capture takes remainders.

ante.reason: Basra is a traditional fishing game where points are accumulated without a pre-hand wagering requirement.

deal.reason: The system automated dealer handles the distribution of four cards to players and the floor at the start.

reveal_market.reason: There is no separate market; cards are played directly to or captured from the central floor tableau.

buy_market.reason: Players do not buy cards from the table; they capture them through rank matching or numerical summation.

buy_stock.reason: The deck is distributed in fixed rounds of four cards; players cannot pay to draw extra cards from the stock.

fold.reason: Players must play all cards in their hand to complete the round; there is no option to abandon the hand early.

check.reason: The game does not feature a betting structure with checks; every turn requires a card to be played to the floor.

call.reason: There are no pots or bets to match; progress is measured strictly by point values of captured cards.

bet.reason: Basra is scored via card accumulation and bonuses rather than through the wagering of chips or currency.

raise.reason: There are no stakes to increase; the competitive element is focused on maximizing captures and Basra bonuses.

declare.reason: Results are calculated automatically based on the cards in the score pile; no separate declaration is needed.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until cards are played; there is no full-hand reveal phase at the end of the round.

award_pot.reason: Winning is determined by cumulative point totals on a scorecard rather than awarding a physical pot.

play_card.description: Play a card to capture by rank or sum, or build table.
play_card.constraints: Match rank or sum to capture; or add to table.

draw.reason: Cards are distributed by the dealer in discrete batches of four rather than through a player draw action.

discard.reason: Cards played without a capture remain on the floor as live cards; they are not discarded to a waste pile.

pass.reason: Players must play exactly one card from their hand every turn until their hand is completely exhausted.

bid.reason: Basra does not utilize an auction or bidding system to determine the dealer or game objectives.

meld.reason: This is a fishing game based on capture mechanics rather than the formation of sets or sequences in the hand.

go_out.reason: The hand ends automatically once all players have played their four cards and the stock is empty.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Players receive cards in fixed batches of four from the dealer at intervals until the deck is gone.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards played to table or captured; no separate discard or recycling pile exists in the game.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Certain ranks (Jacks and 7 of Diamonds) trigger sweeping captures rather than secondary engine effects.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: The result of each play is immediate and public; no hidden declaration phase is required.
notApplicableReasons.trickConfig: Basra is a fishing game based on tableau capture rather than a trick-taking competition.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Goal is to capture table cards and score points; hands are refilled from stock, not emptied as in shedding games.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; points are awarded for capturing specific cards and sweeping the table (Basra).
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for Basra (fishing game) where the ace counts one point in captures and the ten and seven of diamonds score bonus.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Diamonds are significant: the ten and seven of diamonds award extra points when captured. Suits do not affect matching; cards capture by rank or by building to a total.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit (ace through king). The jack can sweep the table; the seven of diamonds has special sweeping power. Ace counts one point; numeric cards may build to a sum for capture. Standard rank order for building.
engine.dealPattern: Initially 4 cards each and 4 to the floor; thereafter 4 cards each until deck empty.

hero.title: BASRA
hero.subtitle: The Egyptian Sweep
hero.tagline: Calculations. Captures. The Komi takes it all.

synthesis.shortDescription: The definitive Middle Eastern fishing game. Use simple addition to capture piles of cards, or slam down a Jack to clear the floor. But watch out—if you leave a single card alone, your opponent might just score a 'Basra' and ruin your lead.

prompts.human: The floor has a 5, an Ace (1), and a 2. You hold an 8. 5+1+2 = 8! Play your 8 to capture all three. Or drop your Jack to sweep everything. Choose wisely—the Basra bonus is at stake.
prompts.ai: Game: Basra. Type: Fishing. Rules: Match Rank or Sum. Jack takes all. 7♦ takes all. Clear table = Basra (+10 pts). Points for cards + Basras.

scoring.description: Points are tallied at the end of the game (deck exhaustion).
scoring.winCondition: First to reach 101 or higher (or highest score after fixed rounds).
scoring.splitRules: If cards are equal (26-26), the 30 points for Carte are not awarded.
